text:
jon: heads-up — we've been seeing bursts cause ~30% more late-credit records in the billing ingest. thinking we need a topology-level fallback plus client-side rate smoothing.

maria: can you paste a quick example of the burst pattern?

jon: log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-19T18:11:03Z INFO request=abc123 tenant=acme tokens=1024 latency_ms=18
2026-03-19T18:11:04Z INFO request=abc124 tenant=acme tokens=5000 latency_ms=25
2026-03-19T18:11:04Z WARN ingress_buffer_full tenant=acme queued=120
2026-03-19T18:11:05Z ERROR credit_write_late request=abc124 shard=42
```

kevin: ugh. sounds like the transient ingress backlog causes our handshake to race and the attribution record lands in a different partition. that explains late-credit duplicates.

lee: quick idea: add a short smoothing window on the client SDK that spreads token emission across 200–500ms when request rate > X per second. reduces microbursts.

maria: SDK smoothing helps but we still need server-side fallback. otherwise a noisy tenant will overwhelm a shard and push its events to the fallback path which currently doesn't preserve provenance well.

jon: exactly. proposal: (1) client-rate-smoothing opt-in flag in SDK, (2) ingress topology change: per-tenant circuit breaker + local buffer with soft-lease (100ms) before falling back to cross-shard queue, (3) when fallback occurs, attach provenance header and origin-offset to the fallback event so we can reconstruct ordering for audit.

kevin: tradeoffs: adding soft-lease increases tail latency for some requests (100ms extra) but should reduce duplication and audit churn. attaching provenance header will bloat event size — ~40 bytes — but worth it for reconciliations.

lee: how do we handle retries? if client uses exponential backoff that interacts with the smoothing window, we might amplify smoothing. maybe smoothing should be aware of retry semantics (don't re-smooth retried payloads).

maria: also need to consider charge timing. Customers expect near-real-time billing; a 100ms server buffer is fine but any longer and it changes SLOs. Ops: set alert if smoothing drops >5% throughput for >1m.

jon: sketch of fallback event envelope: 
```
{ "orig_ts": "168...", "origin_shard": 21, "origin_offset": 4321, "provenance": "handshake-v2" , "payload": {...} }
```

kevin: that feels good. for audit pipeline we can use origin_shard+offset as canonical ordering hint during reconciliation. we should also add a reconcile flag so billing-runner knows this came from fallback and needs idempotency checks.

lee: ops question — does this require new indexes in the audit DB? we might need lookups by origin_shard+offset. cost: extra index on big table.

maria: yep. add an append-only provenance index with TTL 90 days. cheap-ish and gives us a deterministic source of truth for late credits.

billing-bot: note: flagged for billing-team review — this change affects billing ingestion semantics. Will create a PRD.

jon: next steps: I'll prototype the ingress soft-lease + provenance header today, and put a feature flag + canary for one tenant. maria — can you coordinate index sizing with data infra?

maria: on it. will share rough storage estimate by EOD.

kevin: i'll update SDK RFC with smoothing opt-in + no-resmooth-on-retry rule.

lee: add a runbook item for fallback-detection and telemetry (metrics: fallback_rate, smoothing_latency_p99, provenance_index_miss).

jon: awesome. if we get these in this week we can avoid a bigger backfill in next billing cycle. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — tagging @billing-team in case anyone wants context.

kevin: sgtm.
